On August 26, a Ukrainian drone targeted the dry spent nuclear fuel storage facility at the ZNPP – damaging it could have led to a serious radiation accident . There are other examples of Zelensky and his clique engaging in increasingly reckless actions , demonstrating to the world their readiness to undermine the nuclear safety of Europe’s largest nuclear power plant and provoke a nuclear disaster. ☝️ Such actions would be impossible without the constant support that Western countries provide to the Kiev junta . It is precisely this support that instils in the criminal regime the false hope of impunity and encourages further reckless actions. ❗️ We once again call on the IAEA leadership to acknowledge the gravity of the situation and take comprehensive measures to exert pressure on Kiev .

On August 27, continuing a good tradition, the staff of the Embassy of Russia visited
Bophelong Children’s Home
in Mamelodi, Pretoria.
The children were treated to traditional Russian sweets, including blini (Russian pancakes) and khvorost, and received a selection of gifts from the Embassy: sporting equipment, school and arts-and-crafts supplies, hygiene products and sweets.
The children were also presented with Russian caps featuring Russian symbols - a particularly practical gift as the South African summer approaches.
Addressing the children and staff of the Home,
Ambassador of Russia to South Africa
Roman Ambarov
stressed the importance of sport, teamwork and perseverance:
“
Among the items we are donating are arts and crafts supplies and sporting equipment, including footballs. These soccer balls are more than sporting equipment - they are symbols of teamwork, discipline and perseverance.
South Africans recently had every reason to celebrate the remarkable performance of Bafana Bafana at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The team’s success inspired millions across the country and showed what can be achieved through hard work, unity and belief in one another. Perhaps one of these footballs will one day be kicked by a future Bafana Bafana player.”
For the Embassy, such visits are not about symbolic gestures or formal occasions.
They are about sincere care, human warmth and the friendship we wish to share with our South African friends.
As Nelson Mandela once said:
“There can be no keener revelation of a society’s soul than the way in which it treats its children.”
And sometimes, friendship is expressed in the simplest things: playing games together, sharing a cup of tea, talking about the little things — and, most importantly, knowing that you are not forgotten.
❤️
Russia and South Africa united by friendship, solidarity and care for the future generation.
#RussiaSouthAfrica

💬
Russia's Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova
:
Former The Guardian correspondent
Saeed Kamali Dehghan
has admitted
that
he fabricated
a 2010 article
presented as an “exclusive interview” with Iranian woman
Sakineh
Mohammadi Ashtiani
, who had reportedly been sentenced to death by stoning.
The article
appeared
on the front page on August 6, 2010,
triggering an international outcry
: Western politicians demanded that the woman be freed, while Iran came under diplomatic pressure from several countries.
👉
Dehghan now
admitted
:
“I want to come clean about a front-page story I wrote for the Guardian.
It was presented as an exclusive interview with Sakineh Ashtiani. That interview never happened. I fabricated the entire piece. It was a false story – completely untrue – and I take full responsibility”.
The article is
still available
on The Guardian website
without any relevant note or retraction.
The context here is important:
the article appeared at a time of intense pressure on Iran – the same year, the UN Security Council adopted
Resolution 1929
, imposing what were then the toughest sanctions against the country.
The West needed an emotionally charged story to justify the sanctions regime
. A woman sentenced to death by stoning was the perfect image. The story immediately spread across the global media and became an argument for those pushing for Iran’s isolation.
This is not the first time Saeed Kamali Dehghan has admitted that
, while working for Western media outlets,
he took part in anti-Iran propaganda campaigns
. In 2020,
he disavowed his involvement in HBO’s documentary For Neda
, about the death of
Neda Agha Soltan
during the 2009 protests, saying that he had been
“influenced by Western narratives”
. The former contributor
described
the film, once held up as a landmark documentary about state violence, as anti-Iran propaganda.
***
☝️
As for Western falsehoods, Dehghan’s admission is far from the first such revelation.
In October 1990, a 15-year-old Kuwaiti girl named
Nayirah
appeared before a US Congressional caucus
. In tears, she claimed that Iraqi soldiers had stormed Kuwaiti hospitals, removed babies from incubators and left them on the floor to die. President George H.W. Bush repeatedly cited her account.
The story became one of the arguments used to build support for Operation Desert Storm.
Two years later, it emerged that
Nayirah
was the daughter of Kuwait’s Ambassador to the US and that
her appearance had been orchestrated by PR agency Hill & Knowlton
, hired by the Kuwaiti government in a multimillion-dollar campaign. The notorious incubator story was never substantiated.
A child was made to tell a lie in order to help justify a war.
In 2003,
The New York Times fired journalist Jayson Blair
after it emerged that
he had invented sources, fabricated quotes and entire reports
, including stories written without ever leaving his New York apartment.
Of 73 articles
reviewed by the newspaper, 36 contained evidence of journalistic misconduct
.
Stephen Glass of The New Republic
fabricated
27 of the 41 articles he published between 1995 and 1998
– inventing characters and companies and even creating fake websites to deceive fact-checkers.
And, of course,
there is the infamous “Powell's test tube”
– a byword for Western deception used to justify aggression against a sovereign state.
Now the Saeed Kamali Dehghan case joins this inglorious list
.
👉
It will certainly not be the last.
Shall we talk about Bucha next
– and how the BBC helped spin that fake?
#DebunkingFakes

🎙
Interview
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov with RBC TV
(Moscow, August 28, 2026)
Key points
:
•
The world is undergoing a transformation, profound changes
. These changes will most likely span an entire era, so the generation currently living on Earth may not necessarily see the final configuration that emerges.
• After the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the West always had the idea of
“keeping Russia close”
–
but not as an equal partner
. Even when we triumphantly joined the G8, which later reverted to the G7,
our membership was never fully equal
.
• The turning point in our attitude, when we finally understood and became convinced that
the West had no intention of cooperating with us on an equal footing
, was
President Vladimir Putin’s Munich speech in 2007
. Everyone knows it very well.
• As President
Vladimir Putin
has already said
, we will always be ready for dialogue, but
we have learned our lessons, and
our relations with the West will never again be what they were before February 2022
.
• The recent visits to Moscow by the Vatican’s top diplomat and the CIA Director reflected
the desire of those who came here to visit and talk
.
• I
held talks
with Archbishop
Paul Richard Gallagher
, Secretary for Relations with States and International Organizations of the Holy See.
There was nothing secret about our meeting
. We spoke about virtually everything at
the subsequent press conference
.
• Like everywhere else in the world, Russia has established rules governing interaction between intelligence services. There is nothing unusual about this.
Nor is there anything unusual about such work being conducted discreetly.
• Much of diplomacy, too, takes place behind the scenes,
but diplomats
, by tradition and by the very nature of their profession, are expected to say something publicly. Naturally,
we do not disclose details that are particularly sensitive or still being worked out
, where it is important not to jeopardise possible compromises or consensus.
• The Zelensky regime
shells schools, children’s centres, beaches and passenger buses
– a vast number of facilities that have nothing whatsoever to do with military capabilities.
And the West keeps shamefully silent
. Regrettably, UN Secretary-General
Antonio Guterres
and UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
Volker Turk
are equally silent.
☝️
They have unequivocally and firmly sided with the Ukrainian regime
.
• Geopolitically and geoeconomically, giants such as
China, India and Brazil are asserting themselves and rapidly strengthening their economic standing
, taking their rightful place in global economic affairs.
•
Fundamental changes are taking place in Africa
as the continent begins moving away from
the neocolonial model
under which raw materials were extracted there while value was added in Europe.

item.title: 🗓 On August 27, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met with Anna Tsivileva, Chair of the State Foundation for Support of Participants of the Special Military Operation
item.description: 🗓 On August 27, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met with Anna Tsivileva, Chair of the State Foundation for Support of Participants of the Special Military Operation “Defenders of the Fatherland,” and combat veterans taking part in the annual forum Together We Will Win. During the informal conversation, Sergey Lavrov spoke in detail about the current challenges facing Russian diplomacy and the country’s foreign policy priorities. The Minister warmly thanked the veterans for their courage, valour, and sincere devotion to the Fatherland on the front lines. ❗️ The meeting participants expressed confidence that, despite the West’s ongoing hybrid war against Russia and its extensive support for Ukraine, all the goals of the special military operation will be achieved. Answering questions, Sergey Lavrov detailed the Ministry’s efforts to support participants in the special military operation. He outlined plans for further development of the professional retraining programme, which has been implemented since 2024 at the Main Directorate of the Ministry of Defence and MGIMO University, in collaboration with the Defenders of the Fatherland Foundation. The programme is aimed at the social integration and employment of trainees in the civilian sector. Following the fourth stage of the programme, completed in July 2026, it is planned to expand the number of participants and the scope of the courses, taking into account feedback from graduates.

item.title: ⚡️ Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Rodion Miroshnik On August 26, the Kievsky District of Donetsk
item.description: ⚡️ Ambassador-at-Large of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Rodion Miroshnik : On August 26, the Kievsky District of Donetsk was attacked with Storm Shadow/SCALP-EG missiles. Eight people were injured, including two children. According to the head of the Donetsk People’s Republic , the district was struck with British-French long-range air-launched Storm Shadow/SCALP-EG cruise missiles . The main strike hit the area around the Donetsk City shopping and entertainment center . A girl born in 2016 and a woman born in 1973 sustained moderate injuries. Also injured were a teenage girl born in 2010, a woman born in 1947, and four men born in 1987, 1981, 1977 and 1949. As soon as the British PM spoke of sharing the technology behind these missiles with Kiev , they were used against civilian targets. ❗️ Ukrainian terrorists behave like drug addicts – once they get their hands on something, they rush to use it, usually in the most dangerous way possible for those around them.
